progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: From B4: A pairs with T, C with G; antiparallel strands with 5' and 3' ends; each original strand is a template; semi-conservative copying; a surviving error becomes a changed pair after the next copy. From B6b: template versus coding strand; mRNA is built 5' to 3' and matches the coding strand with U for T. From B6c: codon chart with mRNA codons only; start AUG; stop codons add no amino acid. From B5a: count chromosomes by centromeres; DNA is copied in interphase into two sister chromatids. From B5b: meiosis I separates homologous pairs, meiosis II separates sister chromatids; crossing over swaps matching pieces between non-sister chromatids and makes new combinations of existing alleles; four cells from one. Not assumed: DNA mass per cell (introduced in Q3 as "the DNA follows the chromatids"), linkage frequencies (B8, later in the route; Q4 reasons only from one cell).
progression.startsWith: The hook: Exam questions on DNA and meiosis rarely ask you to recite the steps. They hand you something new, a sequence written from its 3' end, a copying error, a cell you've never seen, and ask you to trace it.
progression.stopsAfter: tracing a copying error through two rounds and counting the changed molecules; turning a coding strand written 3' to 5' into mRNA with ends and an amino acid chain that stops at a stop codon; tracking chromosome number and DNA mass through meiosis; listing the four products of one meiosis with one crossover and explaining why new combinations are less than half of a plant's gametes.
progression.nextLesson: proteins, phenotype and gene-environment interaction (route entry bio-m5-b07).

teaching.task: When a question hands you a sequence or a cell you have never seen, what do you check first so the trace comes out right?
teaching.causalExplanation: Why only one molecule changes (each strand templates its own partner; the T strand keeps the right base) (2b, 2c); why the mRNA is a copy, not a pair, of the coding strand, and why direction matters (mRNA read from 5') (3b); why GGC is not read (stop codon releases the chain) (3c); why copying doubles DNA but not chromosomes (sister chromatids share one centromere) (4b); why meiosis I halves chromosomes but not chromatid count per chromosome (4c); why only two products are new (the crossover joins two non-sister chromatids) and why the plant's overall share is lower (crossovers between these genes happen in only some cells) (5b to 5d).
teaching.conversationalApproach: Opens on the hook (hook), then works through q1-question (question 1: a copying error), q1-first-copy (round one), q1-second-copy (round two), q1-mistake (the classic mistake), q2-question (question 2: a strand written backwards) and the remaining scenes in order, with each reasoning stage shown on its own cue; ends with the unseen attempt (10 second countdown), brief feedback, the decision rule or board, and the key notes.
teaching.openingDecision: Exam questions on DNA and meiosis rarely ask you to recite the steps. They hand you something new, a sequence written from its 3' end, a copying error, a cell you've never seen, and ask you to trace it.
teaching.understandingCheck: Four, each 10 s with the countdown and every demand and condition visible (2a, 3a, 4a, 5a). Nothing answer-bearing during the holds; the checklist strip dims.
teaching.curriculumScope: Syllabus (2017, BIO12-12, programme/syllabus/bio-2017-y12.json, p 49). B5-IQ2-01 "model the processes involved in cell replication, including but not limited to:" with "mitosis and meiosis (ACSBL075)" and "DNA replication using the Watson and Crick DNA model, including nucleotide composition, pairing and bonding (ACSBL076, ACSBL077)"; B5-IQ3-02 "model the process of polypeptide synthesis, including: (ACSBL079)" with "transcription and translation"; B5-IQ4-02 "model the formation of new combinations of genotypes produced during meiosis, including but not limited to:" (the crossing over part only); and, for the crossing over skill by name (Revision 2), B5-IQ4-01 "conduct practical investigations to predict variations in the genotype of offspring by modelling meiosis, including the crossing over of homologous chromosomes, fertilisation and mutations (ACSBL084)", whose practical coverage stays with P01 and P02. Practice and transfer only: the ledger rows stay with their core videos (B4, B5b, B6b, B6c, B8); G01 adds a practice row, not first coverage.

design.visualSystem: One practice board throughout, in the G03c layout: top-left the short task line, kept until the answer lands; under it the stimulus strip (sequence, cell or chromosome); under that the grouped givens card; the working fills the right two thirds; the type badge sits top-right ("Replication", "Transcription and translation", "Meiosis: counts", "Meiosis: alleles"). A trace checklist strip on the far left carries three rows, "which strand?", "which end?", "what am I counting?", and ticks the row each question used. It dims to an outline during every countdown. Earlier questions are cleared before the next card writes on.
design.transitionPlan: One practice board persists: the shared question card sits at the top left and each question clears the working area and writes on its stimulus; working scenes add one reasoning stage at a time, the classic-mistake chip crosses out at the end of each question, and the next question card slides in; the decision board gathers the four methods before the notes; scene crossfade with settle.

Right: the blue T strand picks up a new green A (tick, "normal"); the green G strand picks up a new C, and the pair "G = C" locks in with an amber ring. On "one" the four outlines fill: "normal", "normal", "normal", "G-C: changed", and the answer line writes on: "1 of 4 molecules: G-C in place of T-A".
